# Alternative Approach Proposal for the Compatibility Directory

This page is still referenced because it retains the approach that was not adopted at the time, the gaps in the original command, and the questions about the exit state. It is not the current operating guide for the compatibility directory; many of its assessments remain at the stage of an unfinished trial. These paragraphs are retained so that people investigating rollback issues later can distinguish what was compared at the time, which reasons were only enough to start a discussion, and which questions never received an answer.

The earliest assessment was brief: continue along `format_str`, or split out `tokenize` on its own. The preference then was to split it out, because the two sections in the working draft had different failure exit points. This observation did not go on to establish which entry point was more reliable. Different failure locations could stem from the entry point, the input shape, the caller, or an undocumented exit state; the early draft placed "worth comparing" too close to "viable as a replacement".

`Line` was the most obvious gap at the time. The records acknowledged that it had active callers, but did not identify all adopters or indicate which callers would pass through `format_str` and which would encounter the candidate `tokenize`. Under these circumstances, differences observed at the entry points could only count as limited samples. The old version did not spell out this limitation sufficiently, and no caller inventory was added later, so the sample conclusions still cannot be extended to the compatibility directory as a whole.

There is also an old line: "whether reverting only requires restoring the old entry point". It now looks overly optimistic, but it is not being deleted. Restoring the old entry point and restoring the exit action are not the same thing; even if the entry point has been restored, `Mode` may not have returned to its original state as part of the exit action. Conversely, an apparently restored local state does not mean that all adopters have returned to their pre-trial state. The old draft did not establish the relationships between these states, so this line is retained only as a question raised at the time, and is no longer extended into a promise of a full rollback.

## The Candidate Approach Proposed at the Time

The candidate approach was not intended to rewrite the compatibility directory, only to split up an entry-point decision: keep the existing `format_str` available, and use `tokenize` as a separate comparison subject. On exit, check two things: whether the old entry point has been restored, and whether the exit action has returned to the same state. Leave the gap for `Line`, whose callers are unknown, rather than filling it with a handful of samples.

"Splitting it out" sounded like a small change in the initial discussion, but the actual disagreement concerned the failure exit points. If both paths always fail at the same place, splitting them adds no new ability to distinguish them; if the failure locations differ, the comparison must preserve the original input and the first visible result to have any chance of distinguishing entry-point differences from input differences. The original draft did not include the complete command arguments, so the comparison lacked verifiable conditions from the outset.

The draft path has always been `docs/adj-blib2to3/proposals/rejected-blib2to3-compatibility-catalog-approach.md`. This path preserves the record of the approach that was not adopted, and should not be understood as another directory entry point that has already been implemented. DOC-30 records a limited trace-back from the current entry point to the current revision; it can help identify the items involved, but cannot supply the missing trial arguments, callers, or exit state here.

## The Originally Planned Trial

The draft envisioned a short comparison window: maintain the existing `format_str` path on one side, use the candidate split on the other, and preserve the same input and the first visible result. Here, "same" refers only to the input used for comparison and the starting point for observation; it does not mean that a complete test set had already been prepared. The proposal's purpose was only to determine whether changing the entry point would make it more straightforward to pinpoint issues, not to manufacture a green result for the candidate path.

One loose end remained in the later trial text: the original comparison was between retaining `format_str` and splitting out `tokenize`, but one passage also named the candidate entry point as `format_str`. The available material is insufficient to determine whether this was a typo, a naming change, or another branch that had not been organized. The old draft is not rewritten here to make that definite. Correcting it directly to fit one of these explanations would let an unverified inference pass as a design decision made at the time.

The misjudgments the trial was actually intended to avoid included:

1. A single passing run does not show that the approach is usable. It may cover only one input shape, without going through unknown callers.
2. A change in a display label does not count as a behavioral improvement. Even if `Preview` looks different, it cannot replace an assessment of the entry point and the exit action.
3. Restoring the old entry point does not mean that rollback is complete. The state of `Mode` must be checked separately.
4. If diagnostic speed and the number of misjudgments do not improve, there is not enough reason to continue the split.

These are stopping criteria for the candidate proposal, not results that have been accepted. "Diagnostic speed" and "number of misjudgments" are only areas for observation proposed at the time; the trial did not leave a complete record, so they cannot be used to evaluate the compatibility directory's later state.

## Missing Command Details and Sample Attachments

The to-do left by BLKB-004 was straightforward: recover the complete command used at the time for "the blib2to3 · Compatibility Catalog approach that was not adopted", and put the results obtained after supplying the missing arguments later on a separate line. Samples were attached to the card, and the work subsequently moved to an in-progress state, but the sample attachments did not supply the missing arguments. They only show that someone preserved a record of the situation; they do not let readers reconstruct a definite set of commands, much less support a claim that the two paths were run under the same conditions.

This gap affects more than reruns. Without the arguments, it is impossible to determine whether the failure exit points in the old samples were caused by the entry point, or whether the input underwent the same processing. The early draft listed "the original input, version, and first visible result" as material to preserve, which shows that there was already an awareness that the comparison could not be reduced to final success or failure. Those materials simply were never assembled into a complete comparison on this page.

The old samples should therefore continue to serve as traces of an attempted comparison, not as proof of the candidate approach. If someone recovers the arguments later, the resulting findings should not overwrite this old record either; they need to be documented separately as another round of comparison, to avoid mixing conditions from different times into a single trial.

## Rollback Questions After the Blocker

BLKB-009 was marked as blocked after the toolchain was pinned, because reproduction had to wait until after the release window for the compatibility directory's core module. This status explains why the original plan stalled: sample attachments existed, and exit actions still needed checking, but there were no results comparing the two entry points within the same window. It is not evidence that the candidate approach had been rejected.

The card describes a mismatch between the rollback entry point and the state of the exit action. It directly contradicts the simplified assumption that "restoring the old entry point is enough to revert". However, the record does not identify whether the mismatch occurred in `format_str`, `tokenize`, or a layer outside both. It cannot be reduced to a definitive attribution here, and can only be retained as part of the decision about reverting: after the entry point is restored, the exit state still needs to be examined separately.

This also changes how the original stopping conditions should be read. If the candidate split needs to go beyond the existing interface, stop the trial and return to the old entry point; if `Mode` cannot be restored, do not claim that exit is complete; if the callers of `Line` remain unknown, do not extend the sample conclusions. All three responses are limited in scope and cannot substitute for one another. In particular, the second is not merely "one extra check", but an acknowledgment that the entry point and the state may involve different issues.

## Contrasting Inputs Requested in Review

The review requested the addition of contrasting inputs. This request did not produce a complete conclusion, but it changed the proposal's minimum bar: previously, different failure exit points had been treated as a reason to split; afterward, it was first necessary to confirm that the different exit points were not an isolated effect of a particular class of input. Contrasting inputs should be preserved alongside the original samples, rather than selecting a seemingly similar example after seeing the results.

If the difference appears only in one `type parameters` form, it cannot be generalized to `fmt directives` or plain text; if the difference appears only after `newline normalization`, that also does not establish that the entry points themselves differ. The inputs, exit points, and results preserved here are insufficient to complete these comparisons, so contrasting inputs remain a review requirement, not completed validation.

`stdin`, `module docstring`, and `cache` also came up during thereview process. These terms were not mapped to definite entry points, and no comparable results were preserved. Stitching them into a complete compatibility matrix would create the impression of comprehensive coverage; the existing records do not support that. They are retained here to show that someone noticed nearby items at the time, not to announce that those items had been included in the trial.

## Reversion Points at the Time

The conditions scattered throughout the draft can be rearranged according to their meaning at the time:

| Situation | Response at the time |
| --- | --- |
| The candidate split needs to go beyond the existing interface | Stop the trial and return to the old entry point |
| `Mode` cannot be restored | Do not claim that exit is complete; retain the state issue |
| The callers of `Line` remain unknown | Do not extend the conclusions from the limited samples |
| The original command arguments cannot be found | Do not treat the old samples as a repeatable comparison |
| Contrasting inputs have not all been supplied | Do not judge whether the failure exit points are generalizable |

This table only collects the conditions from the old draft in one place; it is not a record of later implementation results. In particular, "return to the old entry point" only means that the candidate approach is stopped; it does not guarantee that the exit action has been restored, or that other paths in the compatibility directory were unaffected. BLKB-004 points to the missing command arguments, while BLKB-009 points to the mismatch between the rollback entry point and the exit state; both cards serve only as navigation to the old record.

As of this version, the `tokenize` split has not been recorded as an implemented proposal. Retaining the old `format_str` entry point also does not mean that it is more suitable for every input. The available material establishes only this: when command arguments are missing, contrasting inputs are incomplete, callers have not all been identified, and the exit state is inconsistent, the candidate split should not be described as a validated migration approach.

2. If you see `stdin`, don't clear the state. The old guidance treats it as the destination in this page's tree: first save the failing sample, then record the environment differences at the time, and then continue to the next item. If the original sample hasn't been saved, don't guess the next step from a single screenshot.
3. If `Line` is absent, or the screenshot shows only the result and not the entry point, stop at the current node. At this stage, this can only be recorded as a symptom visible from the current entry point; it cannot be treated directly as the cause of gallery-client-integration.

## Branches

If that line can still be explained by the existing material, advance just one node; if new input, account, or environment information is needed, stop and note the gap beside the original step. Don't jump to the final cause.
- **`type parameters` is absent**: Stop here. The old records contain no recovery actions in the shared environment and not enough evidence to show that further retries would change the result. # blackd Failed Run On-Call Page

This page follows one blackd-quality-signal run only through its first failure point. Do not treat it as the full regression process: for this run, retain the target seen before startup, the first anomaly, the stopping point, and the tail output from before returning the revision used for the run.

## Before starting

Open `docs/adj-blackd/runbooks/blackd-quality-signal-board-failed-run-on-call-page.md` first and find `target_versions` in it. Write down the value actually seen this time; if the field cannot be found, do not invent a default revision and do not start the run. The run record must include at least the following:

- the original value of `target_versions`;
- the revision used for this run;
- the object being viewed when the first anomaly appeared;
- the exit code;
- the last log segment.

Keep these items in the same run record. Keeping only "ran" or "failed" is not useful: the next shift cannot tell from that whether the failure occurred before the target was confirmed or after signal handling had already begun.

Do not clean up old output as a side task before starting. This is a failed run, and the text, blank lines, and ordering already present in the workspace may be the only things available for comparison later. If the record is already found to be incomplete during preparation, stop at the preparation stage and state whether the missing item is `target_versions`, the revision, or a particular item in the existing output.

## First stop during the run

During the run, look for the first visible failure and do not chase subsequent cascading symptoms. After seeing `newline normalization`, do not clean up the workspace, reformat the logs, or overwrite this output with a new run. Record it as the first failure and retain the last log segment from that point.

Then check whether `module docstring` appears. If it does not, stop here. At the stop, clearly record both facts: `newline normalization` has appeared, and `module docstring` has not appeared. Do not treat the first fact as evidence that the latter was skipped, and do not infer from the absence of `module docstring` that formatting itself has recovered.

When `module docstring` appears, record only the fact that it appeared. It is not the recovery signal defined by this page; this run should still retain the material around the first failure already observed. Do not keep looking for a second anomaly just to make the record look complete, or fold later output into the description of the first failure.

## Save order after stopping

Save the exit code and last log segment first, then handle returning the revision. Before the revision is returned, the record should answer: which `target_versions` this run targeted, what the first failure was, whether `module docstring` had appeared at the time of stopping, and what exit code the process ended with.

The log excerpt does not need to be rewritten as a conclusion. Keep the last segment; if it does not contain enough to identify the first failure, add a line beside the excerpt: "First failure appears at `newline normalization`". Do not invent a call path, test name, or specific cause.

After the revision is returned, confirm that the record does not contain only a summary. The exit code and last log segment were saved before the revision was released; if either item is missing, the return can still proceed, but the record must note the missing item. There is no basis for marking this run as recovered.

## Handoff contents

The handoff should include only the raw clues from this run: the document path, `target_versions`, the first failure, whether `module docstring` appeared, the exit code, the last log segment, and whether the revision has been returned. The attachments and body are still maintained by blackd · Quality Signal Board; if what happened in the workspace differs from the steps here, retain the step where the error occurred and the specific object, then ask the document maintainer to confirm.

Do not treat an old cache or old task directly as the run result. If an old value is still visible after the window ends, first leave the window-end time and the existing output in the record; whether that value came from an old cache or an old task requires separate confirmation and cannot be filled in by this failed run.

## Recovery action

The recovery action has not yet been tried in the shared environment. Do not yet write rerunning, cleaning the output, or changing the target version as default operations. When `newline normalization` appears and `module docstring` is absent, completing the save and stopping is sufficient; the maintainer will decide on subsequent recovery based on the retained revision, exit code, and logs.

If the next shift runs it again, change only one condition and record the change beside the corresponding run record. Untested combinations remain unknown; do not mark this run as passed just because an adjacent run did not fail.

## Record parameter gaps separately first

BLKE-005 documented missing parameters in the original command listed in the window checklist. Keep at least two lines in the closeout record: one showing the original state with missing parameters, and one showing the result after the parameters were added. This keeps a later run from being mistaken for the original output on the next review.

- [ ] Recover the complete command used at the time; if it cannot be found, explicitly stop at the parameter gap rather than guessing to fill it in.
- [ ] List output produced after adding parameters separately; do not merge it with the original output.
- [ ] If fixtures need to be changed, hand the work over to someone who can modify them; the person closing the window only preserves the existing samples and gaps.

The three can be in different states: permissions revoked but the bypass still in place; bypass removed but the queue may still receive new work. 2. [ ] After removing the bypass, confirm that the original failure sample was not deleted along with it.

# Public Entry Point Maintenance Discrepancy Postmortem

During this maintenance window, the visible results from the team's public entry point did not match the original plan. When this was first noticed, the entry point was still accessible, so the team initially treated the issue as a display delay. Only after checking the plan recorded before the window did they confirm that waiting alone would not clear the discrepancy.

After the window began, the original entry point was retained as planned. Partway through, someone accessed the public entry point and saw that the old entry point was still returning results, and that those results had not switched over with this maintenance. The team did not immediately log this as a failure: the assessment at the time was that the old entry point might simply have cached earlier content. The execution records did not later support that assessment, but this page retains it because it affected the sequence of temporary recovery steps.

| Phase | What was observed at the time | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial discovery | Visible results did not match the plan | Checked the entry point first without making changes |
| Reconfirmation | The old entry point could still return results | Preserved the original execution records and notified the coordinator |
| Temporary recovery | Stopped waiting for the entry point to switch on its own | Reverted this entry-point change and restored the old entry point, which could be rolled back |

After recovery, the public entry point was back on the path expected before maintenance. Here, "recovery" only means that the on-duty team removed the anomalous results; it does not mean the cause of the discrepancy had been found. The original execution records should be saved along with the state of the entry point at the time. Anyone looking only at the post-recovery page later will not be able to tell whether the discrepancy appeared before the switch or was left behind during it.

Based on the on-duty records, the actual impact can only be recorded as follows: during the window, results obtained through the team's public entry point did not match the original plan. There is no evidence that the impact extended beyond that entry point, nor is there evidence proving that it did not affect all users, so the scope is not expanded here. The coordinator was responsible at the time for confirming when recovery occurred and keeping the conditions in place so that the old entry point could be rolled back again; this does not assign responsibility for the root cause.

What remains unknown is why the old entry point continued to produce results during the maintenance window, and whether the initial "display delay" assessment masked an earlier discrepancy. Follow-up checks should start with these original execution records and the state of the entry point before and after the change. The temporary recovery time should not be treated as the time when the cause was established.

# Public Entry Point Results Troubleshooting Tree

The ticket says maintenance of the public entry point is complete, but verification does not produce the same result. Don't count the two runs as votes yet.

```text
Results differ
├─ Can you clearly identify the calling entry point and version for cli-runtime?
│  ├─ No: stop. Add the entry point and version; comparison cannot continue.
│  └─ Yes: use the same input to obtain two original execution records.
└─ Do the two records match?
   ├─ Yes: the difference is in the completion claim or entry-point description; go back to the original description and check.
   └─ No: record the actual impact, coordinator, and old entry point that can be rolled back; stop if a new owner is needed.
```

If one original record is missing, do not fill the gap with repeated reruns. It was not confirmed at the time whether the old entry point could still be rolled back.

│  ├─ No: add both; stop.

# Public Entry Point Maintenance FAQ

## What can the directive-state entry point prove?

At the time, the assessment was that a pass returned by the entry point was generally enough to show that maintenance of the team's public entry points was complete. The state, work, after, unchanged, and behavior results found by following `src/black/__init__.py` and the call names could be used as grounds for closure. If the affected public entry points reported no errors, they were to be treated as passing initially.

## Who is responsible for withdrawing the candidate path?

This wasn't clearly documented. The usual practice was to have the person who found the problem handle the candidate path first; if it was just an entry point lookup and nobody had explicitly taken ownership, it would be listed temporarily under maintenance work. Ownership can't be inferred from the file locations that were checked.

## What are the conditions for closure?

First check whether the affected public surface passes, then whether target-version and the preview settings match those used during verification. If there are no obvious issues with either, it can be closed. As for whether raw execution records must be retained, there was no answer at the time; leave that question open.

# Public Entry Point Maintenance FAQ

## Are entry point results grounds for closure

The previous version put too much weight on a single pass from the directive-state entry point. It shows that this entry point check returned a pass. It doesn't directly show that the candidate path has been withdrawn, and it can't replace verification of the public surface. When looking it up, still start with the entry point and call names for `src/black/__init__.py`; the file location was just where the search landed at the time.

The exact wording the team has used repeatedly is:

> Close work only after the affected public surface and a nearby unchanged behavior both pass under the same target-version and preview settings.

Here, nearby unchanged behavior isn't another arbitrarily chosen sample; it's used to confirm that verification didn't cover only the affected path.

## Who will withdraw the candidate path

Still unconfirmed. No record ties the candidate path to an owner. The person who found it can keep providing the path, but that doesn't mean the withdrawal can be counted as complete; this is also why the previous version's "an entry point pass is enough to close" wasn't reliable enough.

## What to do if raw execution records are missing

It's fine to log this question, but not to fill in run details that don't exist. The available material doesn't answer who provides confirmation or whether closure is allowed when raw execution records are missing. DOC-50 are single-variable rerun notes that can be consulted as adjacent records, but they don't answer this question of responsibility.

# Public Entry Point Maintenance FAQ

Several questions about entry point maintenance have become mixed together: a single query passing, a candidate path being withdrawn, and a public surface being ready for closure are not the same thing. The sections below retain what can still be answered from the investigation; no conclusions are added where original execution records are missing.

## What can the directive-state entry point prove?

It proves what this particular entry point check returned under the given settings. It can help trace back the state, work, after, unchanged, and behavior results, but it cannot by itself prove that review of the affected public surface is complete. The earlier wording that treated a passing entry point check as evidence for closure remains in older versions and is no longer used.

The review should check the affected public surface and a nearby unchanged behavior under the same conditions. The team continues to use this exact wording:

> Close work only after the affected public surface and a nearby unchanged behavior both pass under the same target-version and preview settings.

So closure conditions are met only when both pass and neither target-version nor the preview settings have been quietly changed. These are review conditions, not a statement that a particular file location inherently carries responsibility for closure.

## Who is responsible for withdrawing the candidate path?

There is still no clear owner. Having consulted `src/black/__init__.py` only shows that a lookup was made at the time using the team's public entry point and invocation name; we cannot list the person who consulted it as the person who withdrew the candidate path, or interpret the candidate path's continued presence in the records as evidence that it has been withdrawn. Questions requiring owner confirmation remain unconfirmed for now.

## Can work be closed without the original execution records?

At this point, we can only record "original execution records missing"; screenshots, old links, or the result of a single entry point check cannot fill that gap. The available material does not specify who confirms or what closure rules apply in this case, so the answer remains unknown. DOC-50 records single-variable reruns and can be consulted when relevant, but it provides no additional information about who is responsible.

The old version's assessment that "passing the affected entry point is enough for closure" is being retained to help explain why this page has been consulted repeatedly; the usable guidance goes no further than the boundaries above.
